upstream: Matcha-TTS zh-en, ModelScope dengcunqin/matcha_tts_zh_en_20251010, pytorch_model_sherpa.bin (the checkpoint model-steps-3.onnx was exported from); model code from the PyPI matcha-tts 0.0.7.2 sdist
status: complete. Re-run end to end on the convert host from the upstream checkpoint: frontend_ids -> export -> onnxslim -> calib -> compile, both graphs fully calibrated (61 sentences) and compiled. Both rebuilt .hbm produce output bit-identical to the shipped builds on the board. See rebuild.

artefacts.matcha_zh_en_dec_t512_int16_nashm.hbm: U-Net decoder, 3 Euler steps compiled in
artefacts.matcha_zh_en_embedding.npy: token embedding table [2190, 192] float32, already scaled by sqrt(192); the lookup runs on the CPU. Written by export.py
artefacts.matcha_zh_en_tokens.txt: tokens.txt from the sherpa-onnx packaging (matcha-icefall-zh-en), unchanged
artefacts.matcha_zh_en_lexicon.txt: lexicon.txt from the sherpa-onnx packaging (matcha-icefall-zh-en), unchanged

encoder.inputs: x_emb [1,192,128] (scaled embeddings, zero past the sentence), x_mask [1,1,128]

decoder.inputs: mu_y [1,80,512] (length-regulated mu_x, zero-padded), y_mask [1,1,512], z [1,80,512] (N(0,1) * noise_scale)
decoder.outputs: mel [1,80,512], de-normalised log-mel, zero past the sentence

submodels.cpu_side: embedding lookup; durations ceil(exp(logw)) * length_scale; length regulation (repeat mu_x column i by its duration); the starting noise z. The graphs are fixed-length; the sentence length lives only in the masks.

quantisation: set_all_nodes_int16 on both graphs, measured — see rejected_builds.

licence.tier: redistributable per the model card, with one thing worth checking (the training data)
licence.detail: The ModelScope model card declares Apache-2.0; the Matcha-TTS code is MIT. The training data is not disclosed: the card says mixed Chinese-English data, fine-tuned from the same author's earlier zh-en model, which was trained with icefall's baker_zh recipe. Whether that recipe's Baker corpus (BZNSYP, non-commercial) is in the data is not stated. Check before a commercial build. tokens.txt and lexicon.txt come from the sherpa-onnx packaging of the same model.

toolchain.python_deps: einops, conformer==0.3.2, diffusers==0.25.0, pillow (diffusers imports it)

C.note: board .hbm against the float ONNX, valid frames only, 19 test sentences (first 12 test texts); decoder fed the float encoder's length-regulated output and N(0,1) noise

cosine.note: A is the compiler's own output cosine on the calibration set. B (.hbm vs .bc) was not run as such; the rebuilt .hbm was compared against the shipped .hbm on the board instead, max |diff| 0. C is the board .hbm against the float ONNX. None of these is the gate: the int8 decoder is unintelligible and two speech-quality predictors still liked it. See task_metric.

float_equivalence.note: The fixed-length rewrite is checked in float by export.py on every export: the padded ONNX pair (encoder -> CPU length regulation -> decoder at 512 frames) against an unpadded run of the untouched PyTorch model, same noise.
float_equivalence.sentences: 29 sentences (the first 20 of the 60 test texts)

task_metric.name: round-trip character error rate: synthesise, transcribe with an ASR model (FireRedASR2), compare to the input text
task_metric.protocol: 60 short robot-reply texts, disjoint from calib_texts.txt, token ids from sherpa-onnx's front end, vocoded with Vocos 16 kHz. Automatic MOS predictors (UTMOS, SQUIM) are NOT a substitute: they scored the unintelligible int8 decoder well.
task_metric.threshold: CER within ~0.2 points of the float model on the CPU
task_metric.measured: float on CPU (sherpa-onnx) 1.61%; int16 encoder + int16 decoder on the BPU 1.73%; int8 encoder 2.85%; int8 decoder 99.4%.
task_metric.durations: Durations are ceil(exp(logw)), so the int16 encoder does not match float frame for frame. On 19 test sentences (147 tokens), run on the board: 30 token durations differ, either tokens whose float duration sits exactly on an integer (many at 2.00; a 0.002 logw error flips ceil by one) or long pause/punctuation tokens of 8-58 frames, where a 1-2% logw error is 1-3 frames (+2 on a 16-frame token, -3 on a 55-frame one). Median |dlogw| 0.005. No sentence's total length moved by more than 2 frames. The round-trip CER is the evidence this is inaudible. Compare mels per token segment, not frame for frame.

measured.note: S100P, BCDL MatchaAcoustic / TextToSpeech, the shipped builds.
measured.end_to_end_note: with the Vocos vocoder on the BPU too; 58 ms for the slowest text (two sentences). Real-time factor 0.0070, or 0.0092 with pauses >= 0.2 s shortened to 0.2x as sherpa-onnx does (less audio for the same work).

rejected_builds.name: int8 decoder
rejected_builds.why: Unintelligible: round-trip CER 99.4%. Mel peaks squashed from ~5.2 to ~3.0; 1378 of 2052 nodes under 0.95 per-layer cosine, attention and feed-forward collapsing to zero or negative; three Euler steps feed the estimator its own output so the error compounds, and mixed precision would have to keep most of it at int16. UTMOS 3.26 and SQUIM 3.97 — both predictors rated it well. Would have saved 8.17 -> 4.78 ms.

rejected_builds.name: int8 encoder
rejected_builds.why: Round-trip CER 2.85% against 1.73%, every extra error a swallowed or doubled character: a small logw error moves ceil(exp(logw)) by a whole frame. Would have saved 1.22 -> 0.85 ms.

rejected_builds.name: encoder with token ids as the input
rejected_builds.why: The compiler quantises a float id input like an activation; it chose a threshold of 127 for a 2190-entry vocabulary, and logw came out at cosine 0.83. The embedding lookup moved to the CPU.

rejected_builds.name: stock fixed-length decoder export
rejected_builds.why: GroupNorm statistics and the additive 0/1 attention mask both depend on the amount of padding, so a 512-frame graph differs from the model by up to 9.96 in log-mel while passing a 'padding content does not matter' check.

graph_rewrites.op: decoder GroupNorm -> GroupNorm over the valid frames only (ceil4(F) at full rate, halved per U-Net level)
graph_rewrites.why: nn.GroupNorm normalises over the whole time axis; the padding's conv outputs are not zero, so the statistics depend on how much padding there is.
scaled_dot_product_attention ADDS a float mask: +1 on valid keys, +0 on padded ones. The bias keeps that over the frames the unpadded model has and excludes the rest.

graph_rewrites.op: mask upsampling with expand + reshape, not repeat_interleave
graph_rewrites.why: With repeat_interleave twice in one graph, torch.onnx tracing froze the attention Reshape at a sequence length of 2.

graph_rewrites.op: embedding lookup out of the encoder graph
graph_rewrites.why: Token ids cannot be a float graph input; see rejected_builds.

graph_rewrites.op: 3 Euler steps and mel de-normalisation inside the decoder graph
graph_rewrites.why: One BPU call per sentence instead of three; the step count is fixed (model-steps-3).

rebuild.note: This recipe re-run end to end on 2026-11-04, OE 3.7.0, in a fresh directory, from pytorch_model_sherpa.bin and the PyPI matcha-tts 0.0.7.2 sdist (byte-identical to the archive the shipped build used), with the in-memory import shims instead of patched sources and freshly installed deps.
rebuild.token_ids: frontend_ids.py reproduced the ids of the original build exactly, for calib_texts.txt (40 texts, 61 sentences) and the 60 test texts (94 sentences).
rebuild.onnx: Both slimmed graphs give max |diff| 0.0 against the shipped build's ONNX on all 94 test sentences (encoder outputs and decoder mel).
rebuild.embedding: matcha_zh_en_embedding.npy byte-identical to the shipped file (md5 9596ac2aee04c2eb4777bd56ce6bf8f1).
rebuild.float_check: padded ONNX pair vs unpadded torch 8.54e-05; stock decoder padded to 512: 9.96; rebuilt torch vs published model-steps-3.onnx 5.67e-04.
rebuild.calibration: All five directories value-identical to the shipped build's calibration set (max |diff| 0.0, 61 samples each); pack() writes them with an extra leading axis, which hb_compile accepts (it reshapes by element count). Both graphs fail batch-8 calibration on a batch-1 Reshape and drop to batch 1, as the shipped build did.

decoder.quant_info: same 2098 thresholds as the shipped build; 202 nodes carry different names (X vs X_output_0) because the shipped decoder ONNX came from an earlier export run, and every node present under the same name has the same threshold
decoder.board: max |rebuilt - shipped| = 0 on 19 sentences, although the .hbm differs in size

rebuild.timing_note: Both compiles shared one GPU with two other hb_compile jobs. Uncontended, the shipped build took ~10 min (encoder) and ~70 min (decoder: 19 min calibrating, 47 compiling).
